summary.oneLiner: First ₹1,000cr revenue year (+157% YoY), record ₹1,400cr order book (1.4x), beat its own raised guidance — but **FY27 is a deliberate "build year" (15–20% growth)** capped by **supply-chain (insulators 18–24mo lead) not demand**; the re-acceleration (>50%) is an FY28 story as new factories come online. Big optionality in **BESS/PCS** and **data-centre** verticals.

one-line thesis: First ₹1,000cr revenue year (+157% YoY), record ₹1,400cr order book (1.4x), beat its own raised guidance — but FY27 is a deliberate "build year" (15–20% growth) capped by supply-chain (insulators 18–24mo lead) not demand; the re-acceleration (>50%) is an FY28 story as new factories come online. Big optionality in BESS/PCS and data-centre verticals.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > IndAS 29 (Turkey hyperinflation): ₹25.7cr non-cash "net monetary loss" booked in Q4 other expenses, depressing reported Q4 margins. Symmetric — earlier quarters had monetary gains. Model Endoks normalized; stable-currency Endoks EBITDA ≈ 32% (32.01%→32.13% YoY despite +150% rev). Q4 also absorbed one-time new Labour Code provisions.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: FY27 revenue growth: muted ~15–20% ("S-curve" build year — new factories not yet productive, 6-month audits; most FY27 growth comes from Endoks).
FY28: back to >50% growth once capacities are online. (Mgmt confirmed Piyush's framing.)

Margins: HV product lines sit at ~33% EBIT; expect a 1–2% short-term dip in Q1/Q2 FY27 from raw-material/geopolitical volatility — pass-through happens with a lag (no price-variation clauses). "Not a big gloomy picture."
BESS/PCS margins: 10–12% at bid today → 17–18% at scale (incl. software).
Order-book target: enter FY28 with ₹1,500–1,800 cr (vs ₹1,400 now).
order book & pipeline: Consol OB > ₹1,400 cr (~1.4x FY26 rev). Split: QP ₹520cr · Mehru ₹430cr · Endoks ₹450cr.
Order inflow last qtr ≈ ₹870 cr gross (mgmt corrected from ₹600; executed ₹300cr same qtr) — mostly QP (HVDC + data-centre) and Endoks (energy storage + automation).
QP bid pipeline >₹1,100 cr (FACTS, renewables, data centres).
Demand visibility: Middle East, Europe, US, Australia — grid modernization, renewable integration, STATCOM, power quality.
segment / subsidiary detail (fy26): Cash flow (Q4): Mehru net cash ₹18cr; Endoks Q4 ≈ ₹136 cr.
growth verticals / optionality: BESS / PCS (power conversion): OB US$31m, targeting US$60–80m FY27 → would be India's largest PCS maker at ~US$80m; "billion-dollar opportunity". Built in Turkey (better price realization + semiconductor volume discounts) to scale before entering India. Competes mainly with Chinese (GE priced too high); software/data-security spec keeps China out of US/EU/India.

Data centres: won an order from a US "big-three" hyperscaler (~₹49cr); started with Microsoft Finland last yr. US data-centre reactor market ~₹1,500 cr/yr. BESS also used as UPS in US DCs (50MW steam-turbine parallels).
GIS: first prototypes Jul–Aug 2026; monetization ~1yr out — expected to compound like prior R&D-led products.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin uplift from richer mix / engineering content; HV lines ~33% EBIT.
Semiconductor sourcing is the PCS moat — volume discounts of 40–50% at US$10–50m scale vs small buys; India semis costly/immature, so Turkey-first.
Raw-material volatility (USD, geopolitics) → 1–2% short-term margin risk, recovered with a lag.
Vertical integration (own cable/CTC manufacturing) to de-risk supply.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): New Sangli factory: commissioning Jul–Aug 2026 (slipped from June; trial production by year-end; project mgrs say Dec–Jan). Peak rev potential ₹1,500 cr. + new HV test lab.
Sangli global coil / HVDC / PCS / CTC / magnet-wire facility — Q3 FY27 commissioning; CWIP ₹73cr.
Mehru: extra oven capacity post-Sep 2026; GIS mfg+testing; ₹17.2cr capex.
Endoks: new BESS/PCS facility at Nigde (Dec 2026); exploring further Turkey expansion.
capital allocation: Enabling resolution to raise up to US$75m — dry powder for intl expansion / acquisitions / tech; not immediate, may draw far less.
Promoters waiving salary (2nd yr) + dividend to conserve cash & minimize dilution; zero-debt philosophy; ₹250cr cash but M&A pipeline larger than cash-in-hand.
M&A focus: power-electronics/battery storage · HV power products · insulators (critical bottleneck).
risks & watch-items: #1: Supply chain = the binding constraint. Insulators (18–24mo lead) + winding conductors. "Execution is the key and not order." Already booked out; can't take more orders until new facility live → growth is capacity-gated, not demand-gated.
IndAS 29 will keep distorting reported QoQ margins (non-cash).
Geopolitics (India–Turkey, Middle East war) — mgmt downplays (16yrs in Turkey; Tata/Mahindra/JSPL/Birla also there).
Q1/Q2 FY27 margin dip (1–2%); new Labour Code one-offs.
Customer concentration: top 10 = 35% of business (per DRHP ~1yr ago).
management quality / tone: Candid & disciplined: explicitly commits to discussing risks; beat raised guidance; walks away from low-margin US transformer bids (won't chase unsustainable transformer capacity).
Strategy = "technology moat + scale moat", invest ahead of demand.

Complementary, not competitive, with ABB/Siemens/Hitachi/GE — they are customers/partners who buy QP's coils & instrument transformers (majors make HVDC transformers in-house). QP competes vs Chinese in BESS.
Competitor TAM benchmarks: Trench Electric (EUR 1.5bn OB), Arteche (~₹3,500cr rev) → "TAM is not the problem, execution is."
non-obvious takeaways: Order book is a misleading growth signal here — supply chain (insulators) caps deliveries; watch execution/capacity, not bookings.
BESS unit economics flip in QP's favour: battery cost expected to halve in 2yrs, so the converter becomes >50% of project cost (today 40–50%; DC apps battery ~5%) — QP makes the converter.
The Turkey base is a deliberate cost/logistics moat (land border to Germany 4 days; US 11 days by sea; raw-material cost ≈ India).
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4 FY26 (this): first >₹1,000cr yr; OB ₹1,400cr; FY27 guide 15–20% (build year), FY28 >50%; BESS OB US$31m→target US$80m; new DC hyperscaler win; Sangli commissioning slipped to Jul–Aug.
Q1 FY27 → (next): check Sangli commissioning, BESS order intake vs US$60–80m, margin dip realized?, OB toward ₹1,500–1,800cr.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.
